say: Step one. Set your ready time, at least 30 to 60 minutes before guests are expected. Photographers and the client will arrive early.

panel.heading: Work backwards from guest arrival
items: List every task with a time

say: Step two. List every task, with a time from your practice sessions.

panel.heading: Work backwards from guest arrival
items: List every task with a time

say: Step three. Decide which tasks run at the same time, with different helpers. Give each helper a photo of the finished zone.

panel.heading: Work backwards from guest arrival
items: List every task with a time

say: Step four. Add a buffer of about 20 to 25 percent for late deliveries, a locked hall, or a missing item.

panel.heading: Work backwards from guest arrival
items: List every task with a time

say: Step five. Add loading and travel time, allowing for Saturday morning traffic. That gives you the time you must leave home.

panel.rule: Ready 30 to 60 minutes before guests. Early guests come.

say: Real candles can set fabric, flowers or hair on fire. Keep them at least 12 inches, about 30 cm, from anything that burns, or use flameless candles. LED lights run cooler next to fabric.

cards.d: Real candles at least 12 inches from anything that burns. Prefer flameless and LED lights.
One extension box per wall socket, no daisy-chaining. Tape cables flat along walls.
Weight and tie stands and arches. Generators run outside, away from doors and canopies.

say: Use one extension box per wall socket, and never plug one box into another. Route cables along walls and tape them flat.

say: Weight every stand and tie arches to fixed points, especially outdoors in wind. Generators make carbon monoxide, so they run outside, away from doors, windows and canopies. At children's parties, pick up burst balloon pieces at once.

say: Before guests arrive, walk the room. Does it match what the client approved? Is it secure? Give each piece a gentle shake. Are walkways and exits clear? Is it neat, with no visible tape? And is it clean?
Then photograph every zone while the room is empty. Those are your portfolio pictures, and your proof.

panel.heading: The final walkthrough
items: Secure: give each piece a gentle shake
Neat: equal drops, no visible tape
Clean: no offcuts or balloon scraps

say: For example, Amaka in Abuja found the hotel's ceiling hooks removed. She dropped the ceiling drape, moved the fabric to two extra backdrop frames, called the agreed contact, and offered a partial refund. Tell clients early, and agree in writing.

panel.heading: When something changes
left: Tell the client as soon as you know
Recommend an option, agree in writing
Change the design, not the safety
right: Post photos that are not yours

say: A silent substitution damages trust more than the change itself. Never improvise fixings from light fittings. And only post photos of work you actually did.

say: Keep one row per job: quoted price and actual costs, planned and actual setup time, client rating out of 5, referrals, and anything damaged or lost.

panel.heading: What Tolu's records showed
items: One row per job: quoted vs actual costs
Every setup ran 15 to 20 percent over
Fix: more garland time, quote valid 7 days

panel.rule: Review monthly. Change one habit at a time.

say: To remember. Plan backwards from the ready time, with a buffer. Control flames, cables, stands and generators. Walk through and photograph before guests arrive. Tell clients about changes early. And keep a job record you review every month.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Plan backwards; add a 20 to 25 percent buffer
Candles away from fabric; generators outside

Tell clients about changes early, in writing
Record quoted vs actual, and review monthly
